name: California
title: California CME Requirements for Physicians (MD & DO) | ClearCME
description: California physician CME requirements: MD/DO hours, renewal cycles, mandatory topics, exceptions and board sources. Verified guidance with practical FAQs.
summary: Both MDs and DOs generally need 50 hours every two years. Different boards set the accepted categories, topic requirements and renewal details. Start with the degree on your California license.

boards.label: MD · Medical Board of California
boards.cycle: Two-year renewal cycle; use your actual license expiration. The MD renewal month follows issuance, not your birthday.
boards.credit: AMA PRA Category 1 or another board-accepted pathway.

boards.label: DO · Osteopathic Medical Board of California
boards.cycle: Two-year license renewal period. Issue-month and legacy birth-month schedules differ; use the board record.
boards.credit: Remaining 30 hours may be AOA or AMA accredited. An AMA certificate does not automatically meet the AOA floor.

MD.detail: One-time 12-hour requirement, due within four years of initial licensure or by the second renewal, whichever comes first. Pathology and radiology specialists are exempt. The alternative opioid-treatment pathway is 12 hours, including eight in buprenorphine or similar treatment; check the alternative pathway’s first-renewal deadline.

DO.detail: One-time 12-hour requirement, due within four years of initial licensure or by the second renewal, whichever comes first. Pathology and radiology specialists are exempt. The alternative opioid-treatment pathway is 12 hours, including eight in buprenorphine or similar treatment; check the alternative pathway’s first-renewal deadline.

topics.title: Schedule II drugs and opioid addiction risk

DO.detail: At least one of the 50 hours must address addiction to Schedule II drugs or opioids at every renewal. This recurring requirement is separate from the one-time pain-management course.

MD.detail: General internists and family physicians whose patient population is more than 25% age 65 or older must devote at least 20% of mandatory CME to geriatric medicine, care of older patients or dementia care.
California requires specified content in qualifying CME. This is not a separate universal extra-hour quota. Check the provider’s California-compliance statement and applicable exceptions.

DO.detail: California requires specified content in qualifying CME. This is not a separate universal extra-hour quota. Check the provider’s California-compliance statement and applicable exceptions.

sections.title: Exceptions and first renewals
paragraphs: Your initial license period, residency or fellowship participation, or specialty-board examination history may affect the usual requirement. Your board’s instructions explain which rules apply to your first renewal.

OMBC permits training-related waivers with documentation from the residency or fellowship program; inactive status and discretionary waivers have separate rules. Ask the relevant board before relying on an exemption.

sections.title: Carryover and documentation
paragraphs: Complete CME within the period immediately preceding your license expiration. Excess hours from an earlier period do not become new training in the next period. Keep proof of one-time requirements available for future renewals.

Keep course title, dates, hours, sponsor, accreditor and completion documentation for at least four years. Both boards can audit. OMBC asks for accepted documentation formats and submission through the instructions provided with an audit.

sections.title: What’s tricky about California
paragraphs: The same 50-hour headline hides different category rules. A DO with 50 AMA hours can still miss the 20-hour AOA Category 1-A/1-B minimum. A course’s topic and its accreditation category are separate checks.

Use the actual board expiration date. MD issue-month renewal and DO legacy schedules make a birthday-based assumption unreliable. One-time training evidence also needs to outlive the current renewal cycle.

sections.title: Change history
paragraphs: Reviewed September 18, 2026. Both boards continue to require 50 hours for a standard two-year renewal, with different category and topic requirements for MDs and DOs. The geriatrics and dementia provision predates 2026.

faqs.question: Do California MDs and DOs need the same number of hours?
faqs.answer: Generally, both need 50 hours per two-year renewal. DOs also need at least 20 AOA Category 1-A/1-B hours and a recurring Schedule II/opioid hour. The degree-specific rules matter as much as the total.

faqs.question: Does my California license renew in my birth month?
faqs.answer: Check your board record. California MD renewal is tied to issuance. California DOs can have issue-month or legacy birth-month schedules; the recorded expiration is the reliable starting point.

faqs.question: Can my existing pain-management course count?
faqs.answer: Possibly. Confirm the course’s content, accepted accreditation, completion date and whether it met the 12-hour requirement or approved alternative. Keep the certificate even after the current CME cycle ends.

faqs.question: Do I owe separate implicit-bias hours in California?
faqs.answer: California’s implicit-bias provision is a course-content standard, not a separate universal hour quota. A generic implicit-bias course alone does not establish that all of your CME meets California standards.

faqs.question: Can I carry extra hours into my next renewal?
faqs.answer: Complete the applicable hours within the board’s current renewal period. Excess hours from the previous cycle do not count as newly completed training.

faqs.question: Does uploading to ClearCME report my hours to the California board?
faqs.answer: No. ClearCME helps organize records. You remain responsible for board renewal attestations and for providing documentation if selected for audit.

sources.label: Medical Board of California · CME, exemptions and records
sources.quote: a minimum of 50 hours of approved Continuing Medical Education (CME) hours during each biennial renewal cycle

sources.label: Osteopathic Medical Board · CME guidance effective October 2025
Business and Professions Code §2190.5 · pain management
Business and Professions Code §2190.6 · alternative opioid pathway
Business and Professions Code §2190.1 · course content
Business and Professions Code §2423 · MD expiration

productNote: Keep California certificates and completion history together. Review the AOA category floor, one-time course alternatives, exemptions and your board’s expiration date separately; ClearCME does not certify those determinations.

name: Texas
title: Texas CME Requirements for Physicians (MD & DO) | ClearCME
description: Texas physician CME requirements: MD/DO hours, renewal cycles, mandatory topics, exceptions and board sources. Verified guidance with practical FAQs.
summary: Texas uses one physician rulebook for MDs and DOs: 48 hours per registration period, at least 24 formal hours, and mandatory topics that run on different schedules. Official CE reporting now runs through CE Broker.

boards.label: MD and DO · Texas Medical Board
boards.cycle: 24-month registration period, rather than the calendar year. Check the expiration on your registration.
boards.credit: Accepted formal pathways include AMA PRA Category 1, AAFP, AOA Category 1-A and TMA-approved activities.

MD.detail: At least two formal hours each renewal period. The activity must have the appropriate ethics or professional-responsibility approval.

DO.detail: At least two formal hours each renewal period. The activity must have the appropriate ethics or professional-responsibility approval.

MD.detail: Physicians who provide direct patient care need two formal hours within one year of initial licensure, again as part of the second renewal, and then every eight years.

DO.detail: Physicians who provide direct patient care need two formal hours within one year of initial licensure, again as part of the second renewal, and then every eight years.

MD.detail: Direct-patient-care physicians need at least one hour in the first renewal period and every third renewal thereafter. Use an HHSC-approved course. An ethics designation alone is not HHSC approval.

DO.detail: Direct-patient-care physicians need at least one hour in the first renewal period and every third renewal thereafter. Use an HHSC-approved course. An ethics designation alone is not HHSC approval.

topics.title: Life of the Mother Act · SB 31

MD.detail: One hour, once, before initial licensure or the first renewal after January 1, 2026 for the applicable specialties. TMB includes obstetric specialties, emergency medicine and family medicine. Only its free MyTMB course satisfies this specific requirement.

DO.detail: One hour, once, before initial licensure or the first renewal after January 1, 2026 for the applicable specialties. TMB includes obstetric specialties, emergency medicine and family medicine. Only its free MyTMB course satisfies this specific requirement.

MD.detail: HB 47 establishes two hours for covered physicians treating patients in emergency settings. Although the statute refers to renewals on or after September 1, 2026, TMB’s current notice says implementation begins with licenses expiring February 28, 2027 because approved coursework is not yet available. Read the live notice and approved-course list before enrolling.

DO.detail: HB 47 establishes two hours for covered physicians treating patients in emergency settings. Although the statute refers to renewals on or after September 1, 2026, TMB’s current notice says implementation begins with licenses expiring February 28, 2027 because approved coursework is not yet available. Read the live notice and approved-course list before enrolling.

sections.title: Exceptions and specialty requirements
paragraphs: TMB describes an exemption for newly licensed physicians at first registration; that does not erase separately timed requirements such as initial opioid training. Retired/voluntary-charity status, residency and board-approved hardship exemptions have their own conditions.
EMS medical directors and pain-management-clinic personnel can have additional requirements. If either role applies to you, review the board’s specialty guidance and current hours chart.

sections.title: Carryover and documentation
paragraphs: Texas permits up to 48 excess hours to carry forward, subject to the board’s two-year limit and category rules. Medical ethics/professional-responsibility and pain-management/opioid hours may not be carried forward.

Complete official reporting and provide certificates through CE Broker before renewal. Keep the certificate, accreditation/category, topic designation and date for every course, including evidence supporting any carryover. ClearCME storage does not submit official CE Broker reports.

sections.title: What’s tricky about Texas
paragraphs: A single renewal date does not mean a single topic clock. Ethics is recurring each cycle; human trafficking follows a three-renewal cadence; opioid training starts early and later follows an eight-year cadence. SB 31 is a separate one-time course.

The MyTMB SB 31 course is not AMA Category 1. TMB allows it toward its ethics requirement; the course completion is recorded in MyTMB. If using it for ethics hours, follow TMB’s CE Broker reporting instructions.

sections.title: What changed in 2026
paragraphs: Mandatory CE tracking through CE Broker began September 1, 2026. A free basic account is available; a paid subscription is not required for official reporting.

SB 31’s first-renewal-after-January-1 deadline applies to the specified specialties. HB 47’s statutory start and the later board rollout notice are both relevant; the current TMB notice controls the operational instructions shown here. Nutrition/metabolic-health training is a separate forthcoming implementation: confirm the final TMB rule before choosing a course or assuming an hour count.

faqs.question: Do I need CE Broker to renew my Texas physician license?
faqs.answer: TMB requires official CE tracking through CE Broker beginning September 1, 2026. Report your courses and resolve discrepancies there before renewal. ClearCME does not replace this official reporting step.

faqs.question: Is CE Broker free for Texas physicians?
faqs.answer: The basic account supports required reporting without a paid subscription. Paid upgrades are optional. Use the account link on TMB’s official tracking page.

faqs.question: How often is opioid CME required?
faqs.answer: For direct patient care, two hours are due within one year of initial licensure and again as part of the second renewal. After the initial requirements, the cadence is two hours every eight years.

faqs.question: Can my existing CME hours count or carry forward?
faqs.answer: Check dates, accepted category and the applicable registration period. Texas permits limited carryover of up to 48 excess hours, but excludes ethics/professional-responsibility and pain/opioid hours from carryover.

faqs.question: Which human-trafficking course satisfies Texas?
faqs.answer: Choose a course on the current HHSC-approved list. The topic library can help you find options. Confirm that your chosen course appears on the HHSC-approved list.

faqs.question: Can one course satisfy more than one Texas requirement?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. TMB permits appropriately designated opioid or human-trafficking training to count toward ethics. Check each required designation, and count the course’s earned hours only once toward your overall total.

faqs.question: Can I take any pregnancy-emergency course for SB 31?
faqs.answer: No. Only the TMB course through MyTMB satisfies this specific requirement. An outside course may count as ordinary CME without meeting SB 31.

sources.label: Texas Medical Board · physician CME and current implementation notices
sources.quote: Mandatory CE Tracking for ALL TMB licensees begins September 1, 2026.

sources.label: Texas Medical Board · continuing education tracking

productNote: Organize certificates and track your recorded Texas requirements. Confirm initial-licensure timing, specialty applicability, carryover and official CE Broker reporting with TMB. ClearCME does not submit your renewal or guarantee course acceptance.

name: Florida
title: Florida CME Requirements for Physicians (MD & DO) | ClearCME
description: Florida physician CME requirements: MD/DO hours, renewal cycles, mandatory topics, exceptions and board sources. Verified guidance with practical FAQs.
summary: Florida generally requires 40 hours per two-year cycle. MDs and DOs answer to different boards, with different renewal dates, category rules and medical-error course requirements.

boards.label: MD · Board of Medicine
boards.cycle: Two years; January 31 in your assigned odd- or even-year group.
boards.credit: General AMA Category I hours and the board’s specifically permitted alternatives.

boards.label: DO · Board of Osteopathic Medicine
boards.hours: 40 hours, including at least 20 AOA Category 1-A
boards.cycle: Two years; March 31 in even-numbered years.
boards.credit: Check AOA designation and the osteopathic board’s mandatory-topic approvals.

MD.detail: Two hours every renewal in a course that meets the Board of Medicine’s content requirements, including its specified high-risk and commonly misdiagnosed conditions.

DO.detail: Two hours every renewal in a course that meets the Board of Osteopathic Medicine’s content requirements. The required conditions differ from those specified for MDs.
One hour each biennium, in addition to the medical-error course.

MD.detail: Two hours each renewal for physicians within the statutory prescribing scope. Use a qualifying board-approved course. Effective July 1, 2026, the required content includes treating pain in patients with sickle cell disease.

DO.detail: Two hours each renewal for physicians within the statutory prescribing scope. Use a qualifying board-approved course. Effective July 1, 2026, the required content includes treating pain in patients with sickle cell disease.

MD.detail: Two hours every third biennium (six years). Track the cycle in which you last fulfilled it.

DO.detail: Two hours every third biennium (six years). Track the cycle in which you last fulfilled it.

MD.detail: One hour by the first biennial renewal. The course must include Florida HIV/AIDS law and meet the rule’s Category I requirements.

DO.detail: One hour by the first biennial renewal, meeting the osteopathic board’s HIV/AIDS course requirements.

MD.detail: One hour, one-time, under section 456.0341. Keep the original completion record. The statute also contains an awareness-sign obligation, which is separate from taking CME.

DO.detail: One hour, one-time, under section 456.0341. Keep the original completion record. The statute also contains an awareness-sign obligation, which is separate from taking CME.

sections.title: First renewal and exemptions
paragraphs: Florida’s first-renewal rules differ from an ordinary 40-hour renewal. The MD board lists HIV/AIDS, medical errors and controlled-substance training for covered DEA registrants. For a DO license, use the osteopathic board’s separate first-renewal rules.
Military service and other narrowly defined circumstances can qualify for board-approved exemptions. Approval of an exemption from general hours does not necessarily waive mandatory topics.

sections.title: Carryover and documentation
paragraphs: Excess CME does not carry forward into the next Florida biennium. Match each course to the correct cycle and retain the full certificate, not only a total-hour tally.

Use the official CE reporting system and check what is recorded before renewal. Keep certificates, approved-provider details and documentation supporting exemptions or prior one-time training; provide records when requested by the board.

sections.title: What’s tricky about Florida
paragraphs: Forty hours can still leave a DO short of the AOA Category 1-A floor. Likewise, a course approved for the MD medical-error requirement may omit the conditions required by the DO board.

The one-time HIV/AIDS and trafficking records, six-year domestic-violence clock and recurring prescribing course should be checked independently. Federal MATE Act training does not automatically replace any Florida-specific requirement.

sections.title: What changed in 2026
paragraphs: The controlled-substance course content changed effective July 1, 2026 to include pain treatment for patients with sickle cell disease. Check that the activity satisfies the current statute and board approval, even if an older certificate has the same course title.
Reviewed September 18, 2026 against the current medical and osteopathic board renewal guidance.

faqs.question: Do Florida MDs and DOs both need 40 hours?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, per two-year cycle, subject to first-renewal and other exceptions. DOs also need at least 20 AOA Category 1-A hours and one hour of Florida laws/rules and ethics.

faqs.question: Can I use an MD medical-errors course for a DO renewal?
faqs.answer: Only if it also meets the osteopathic board’s requirements. The boards specify different content, so check the activity’s approval for your DO license.

faqs.question: Is HIV/AIDS training required every renewal?
faqs.answer: The one-hour requirement is tied to the first biennial renewal. Keep proof of that completion for future renewals. Medical-error and prescribing courses have separate recurring requirements.

faqs.question: Can I carry Florida CME into the next cycle?
faqs.answer: No. Complete the applicable hours in the current biennium; excess hours do not move into the next cycle.

faqs.question: Does MATE Act training satisfy Florida controlled-substance CME?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. The Florida course has its own content and approved-provider requirements, including the 2026 sickle-cell-pain update. Verify any proposed dual use against both sets of rules.

faqs.question: Does ClearCME report to CE Broker or renew my license?
faqs.answer: No. Organizing your certificates in ClearCME is separate from official reporting and renewal. Review the board’s CE record and finish the required reporting before submitting renewal.

sources.label: Florida Board of Medicine · MD renewal and CME
sources.quote: CME hours do not carry over across biennial licensure cycles.

sources.label: Florida Board of Osteopathic Medicine · DO renewal
Florida Administrative Code 64B8-13.005 · MD topics and HIV/AIDS

productNote: Keep certificates and prior mandatory-topic completions in one place. Check first-renewal exceptions, the DO category floor and board-specific course approvals manually. Official CE reporting remains a separate step.

name: New York
title: New York CME Requirements for Physicians (MD & DO) | ClearCME
description: New York physician CME requirements: MD/DO hours, renewal cycles, mandatory topics, exceptions and board sources. Verified guidance with practical FAQs.
summary: New York has no general physician CME-hour minimum, but it does require specific training. MDs and DOs share the same physician requirements, with separate clocks for registration, infection control and prescriber education.

boards.label: MD and DO · New York physician license
boards.cycle: Physician registration renews every two years. Training deadlines are separate.
boards.credit: Required courses must meet the relevant NYSED or NYSDOH approval and content rules.

MD.detail: Two hours of approved training are required for initial licensure unless an accepted education pathway or exemption applies. Previous completion does not remove the updated-curriculum requirement due November 17, 2026.

DO.detail: Two hours of approved training are required for initial licensure unless an accepted education pathway or exemption applies. Previous completion does not remove the updated-curriculum requirement due November 17, 2026.

MD.detail: Complete approved training at initial licensure and every four years, unless a formal exemption applies. NYSDOH oversees the physician training pathway.

DO.detail: Complete approved training at initial licensure and every four years, unless a formal exemption applies. NYSDOH oversees the physician training pathway.

topics.title: Pain management, palliative care and addiction

MD.detail: Three hours every three years for the prescribers covered by Public Health Law 3309-a, including DEA-registered practitioners and covered residents prescribing under an institutional DEA registration. Complete the required NYSDOH attestation as well as the course.

DO.detail: Three hours every three years for the prescribers covered by Public Health Law 3309-a, including DEA-registered practitioners and covered residents prescribing under an institutional DEA registration. Complete the required NYSDOH attestation as well as the course.

sections.title: Exceptions and exemptions
paragraphs: NYSED describes education-based and practice-based exceptions to child-abuse coursework. A low-risk practice setting alone does not establish an infection-control exemption; the appropriate agency determination is required.
NYSDOH has an exemption process for the prescriber requirement. Follow the agency’s documentation and approval process before treating a training obligation as waived.

sections.title: Carryover and documentation
paragraphs: There is no general hour bank to carry into a later New York registration cycle. Recurring training must meet its own interval; keep the completion date for each topic.

Keep authorized course certificates and documentation of any accepted exemption. NYSED specifies submission of child-abuse completion or exemption documentation. Preserve the NYSDOH prescriber attestation confirmation separately from the course certificate.
NYSDOH’s prescriber attestation instructions require keeping training records for six years from submission of the attestation, available for audit or inspection.

sections.title: What’s tricky about New York
paragraphs: “No general CME requirement” does not mean no training. A two-year registration, four-year infection-control interval and three-year prescriber interval will not always align.

The child-abuse requirement is normally one-time, but curriculum updates can require action by physicians who already completed it. Check the version and date of your course, not just whether you have a certificate.

sections.title: What changed in 2026
paragraphs: November 17, 2026 is the deadline for the updated child-abuse curriculum covering identification of abuse or maltreatment of children with intellectual or developmental disabilities.

For approved training completed between November 1, 2022 and August 31, 2025, NYSED describes a 15-minute addendum available through most approved providers. Updated full courses began September 1, 2025. This follows a separate earlier curriculum-update deadline of April 1, 2025.

faqs.question: Does New York require 50 hours of CME for physicians?
faqs.answer: No general physician CME-hour minimum applies. Specific mandated training still applies, and specialty certification, hospital privileges or other licenses may have separate requirements.

faqs.question: Are the MD and DO requirements different?
faqs.answer: New York licenses both under the physician profession. The mandated training described here applies to both degrees, subject to the relevant practice and exemption rules.

faqs.question: Do I need to repeat child-abuse training in 2026?
faqs.answer: You must meet the updated curriculum by November 17, 2026 even if you previously trained. If your approved course was completed from November 1, 2022 through August 31, 2025, check the approved-provider addendum pathway.

faqs.question: How often is infection-control training due?
faqs.answer: Generally every four years after the initial training, unless an approved exemption applies. It is a separate clock from your two-year registration.

faqs.question: Does my DEA MATE Act course cover New York prescriber education?
faqs.answer: Only if the activity independently meets New York’s required content and timing. The federal MATE Act is one-time; New York prescriber education recurs every three years and has its own attestation.

faqs.question: What proof should I keep?
faqs.answer: Keep each certificate, the completed curriculum/version, completion date, approval information and any official attestation or exemption confirmation. ClearCME records do not replace NYSED or NYSDOH submissions.

sources.label: NYSED · physician child-abuse training and November 2026 update
sources.quote: complete the updated training curriculum by November 17, 2026

sources.label: NYSDOH · mandatory prescriber education and attestation
NYSDOH · prescriber attestation and record retention

productNote: Organize the certificates behind New York’s separate training deadlines. Check the 2026 child-abuse curriculum update and complete required agency attestations yourself; ClearCME does not verify a course’s NYSED/NYSDOH approval or submit those attestations.

name: Nevada
title: Nevada CME Requirements for Physicians (MD & DO) | ClearCME
description: Nevada physician CME requirements: MD/DO hours, renewal cycles, mandatory topics, exceptions and board sources. Verified guidance with practical FAQs.
summary: Nevada MD and DO requirements differ substantially. MDs have a biennial specialty-hour requirement and first-cycle phase-down. DOs have a transition: the December 2026 renewal still uses 35 hours from the preceding year.

boards.label: MD · State Board of Medical Examiners
boards.cycle: Biennial renewal on June 30 of odd-numbered years. Newly licensed MDs may qualify for the phase-down below.
boards.credit: AMA PRA Category 1 or board-approved CME; topic and specialty requirements still apply.

boards.label: DO · State Board of Osteopathic Medicine
boards.hours: 2026: 35 hours / preceding year. After 2026: 40 hours / preceding biennium.
boards.cycle: December 31 in even-numbered years. The transition changes the CME lookback, not just the total.
boards.credit: 2026: at least 10 Category 1A hours; later renewals: at least 20. The Nevada rule recognizes AOA- or ACCME-accredited sponsors for this category.

topics.title: Ethics, pain management or addiction care

MD.detail: Two hours every two years in ethics, pain management or addiction care. Qualifying SBIRT training may count toward this requirement; suicide-prevention training does not.

DO.detail: Two hours every two years in ethics, pain management, addiction care or SBIRT. Suicide-prevention training does not count toward the ethics requirement.

MD.detail: Two hours within two years of initial licensure and every four years thereafter. This requirement applies across medical specialties.

DO.detail: Two hours within two years of initial licensure and every four years thereafter. This requirement applies across osteopathic medical specialties.

MD.detail: Two hours once, within two years of initial licensure, for screening, brief intervention and referral to treatment. Keep the one-time completion record.

DO.detail: Two hours once, within two years of initial licensure, for screening, brief intervention and referral to treatment. Keep the one-time completion record.

MD.detail: Two hours every two years for physicians registered to dispense controlled substances in Nevada. Eligible topics include controlled-substance misuse and abuse, opioid prescribing or addiction.

DO.detail: For renewal through December 31, 2026: two hours from the preceding year. For later renewals: four hours from the preceding two years. Eligible topics include controlled-substance misuse and abuse, opioid prescribing or addiction.

MD.detail: Two hours within two years after beginning to provide or supervise hospital emergency services or primary care. This requirement applies to physicians in those practice settings.

DO.detail: Two hours within two years after beginning to provide or supervise hospital emergency services or primary care. This requirement applies to osteopathic physicians in those practice settings.

MD.detail: Psychiatrists need two hours every two years in cultural competency and diversity, equity and inclusion. This requirement is specific to psychiatry.

DO.detail: Osteopathic physicians practicing psychiatry need two hours every two years in cultural competency and diversity, equity and inclusion. This requirement is specific to psychiatry.

sections.title: MD first-cycle phase-down · July 2025–June 2027
paragraphs: Licensed before July 1, 2025 or during July–December 2025: 40 total hours, including 20 specialty/scope hours. Licensed January–June 2026: 30 total and 15 specialty/scope hours. Licensed July–December 2026: 20 total and 10 specialty/scope hours. Licensed January–June 2027: 10 total and five specialty/scope hours.

The two-hour ethics/pain/addiction block is not reduced. NAC 630.157 supplies the total-hour phase-down; the board’s current chart supplies the corresponding specialty/scope numbers. This MD phase-down does not establish a DO proration rule.

sections.title: Exceptions, carryover and documentation
paragraphs: NAC 630.153 provides an MD exemption for a completed residency/fellowship year during the preceding biennium. Inactive-license rules differ from active practice. Confirm the exact pathway and any still-applicable obligations with your board.

Use CME from the applicable lookback rather than assuming unused hours carry forward. Keep certificates, accepted category, specialty/scope content, topic allocation and lifetime-topic records. MDs attest at renewal and can be audited; the DO transition rule requires satisfactory completion evidence.

sections.title: What’s tricky about Nevada
paragraphs: The December 31, 2026 DO renewal requires 35 hours over the preceding year, including 10 Category 1A and two controlled-substance/opioid/addiction hours. Later renewals use 40 hours over the preceding biennium, including 20 Category 1A and four prescribing/addiction hours.

MD first-cycle totals depend on the actual issuance block. Specialty/scope hours and topic-specific clocks add separate checks. ClearCME does not yet calculate all of these adjustments. Confirm your required total and specialty hours with the board before renewal.

sections.title: What changed in 2026
paragraphs: AB 56 moved DO renewal to a biennial schedule. The approved R092-25 regulation, filed July 1, 2026, expressly preserves the annual CME lookback for renewals through December 31, 2026 and changes later renewals.

The former MD bioterrorism/WMD statutory mandate was removed effective January 1, 2026. Older regulatory text and third-party summaries can still show it; the current statute and board chart should be read together.

faqs.question: Is Nevada DO renewal in 2026 based on 35, 40 or 70 hours?
faqs.answer: For renewal on or before December 31, 2026, the approved transition regulation requires at least 35 hours over the preceding year, including 10 Category 1A and two prescribing/addiction hours. The requirement for that renewal is 35 hours, not 70.

faqs.question: When does the 40-hour DO biennium apply?
faqs.answer: The approved regulation applies 40 hours over the preceding biennium to renewals after December 31, 2026, including 20 Category 1A and four controlled-substance/opioid/addiction hours. The next ordinary even-year renewal is December 2028.

faqs.question: I obtained my Nevada MD license in October 2026. What is my first-cycle total?
faqs.answer: The board’s July 2025–June 2027 chart assigns the July–December 2026 issuance block 20 total hours, including 10 specialty/scope hours and the unreduced two-hour ethics/pain/addiction block. Check other applicable topics separately.

faqs.question: Is Nevada suicide-prevention CME only for psychiatrists?
faqs.answer: No. The two-hour suicide-prevention requirement applies generally, first within two years of licensure and then every four years. Psychiatry-specific cultural-competency training is a different requirement.

faqs.question: Do I still need the four-hour bioterrorism/WMD course?
faqs.answer: The former MD statutory mandate was removed. It is absent from the current board chart, although older regulatory language and summaries can still mention it. Use the current statute and board guidance.

faqs.question: Can ClearCME calculate my exact Nevada compliance status?
faqs.answer: ClearCME can organize your certificates and completion history, but it does not yet fully account for reduced first-cycle MD totals, specialty-hour minimums or the DO 2026 transition. Confirm your requirements with the board before relying on a dashboard total.

NRS 630.253, 630.2535 and 630.267 · MD topics and renewal

name: Pennsylvania
title: Pennsylvania CME Requirements for Physicians (MD & DO) | ClearCME
description: Pennsylvania physician CME: 100 hours, distinct MD/DO categories and deadlines, mandatory topics, 2026 organ-donation training and board sources.
summary: Pennsylvania MDs and DOs generally need 100 hours every two years, but their category minimums and renewal dates differ. Organ-donation education now has a separate one-time deadline, while child-abuse reporting and prescriber training remain renewal checks.

boards.label: MD · State Board of Medicine
boards.cycle: January 1 of an odd-numbered year through December 31 of the following even-numbered year. The current regular renewal deadline is December 31, 2026.
boards.credit: The remaining hours may be AMA Category 1 or Category 2. Office management and practice-building courses do not qualify.

boards.label: DO · State Board of Osteopathic Medicine
boards.cycle: November 1 of an even-numbered year through October 31 of the next even-numbered year. The current regular renewal deadline is October 31, 2026.
boards.credit: The remaining hours may use accepted AOA or AMA Category 1 or Category 2 activities. AMA Category 1 alone does not establish the AOA 1-A minimum.

MD.detail: 12 hours per biennial period, within the 100-hour total. Category 1 or 2 activities may qualify. Keep the required child-abuse and opioid hours separate from this 12-hour topic total.

DO.detail: 12 hours per biennial period, within the 100-hour total. Category 1 or 2 activities may qualify. Keep the required child-abuse and opioid hours separate from this 12-hour topic total.

MD.detail: Three hours of approved training for initial licensure, then two hours for each biennial renewal, unless the Board grants a specific child-abuse-training exemption. A general CME exemption alone does not remove this obligation. The approved course provider must report completion electronically to the licensing system.

DO.detail: Three hours of approved training for initial licensure, then two hours for each biennial renewal, unless the Board grants a specific child-abuse-training exemption. A general CME exemption alone does not remove this obligation. The approved course provider must report completion electronically to the licensing system.

topics.title: Pain management, addiction and opioid prescribing

MD.detail: Two hours per renewal for prescribers and dispensers. The exemption requires both exemption from DEA registration and no use of another person’s or entity’s DEA registration to prescribe. These hours count within the total, but not toward the 12-hour risk-management requirement.

DO.detail: Two hours per renewal for prescribers and dispensers. The exemption requires both exemption from DEA registration and no use of another person’s or entity’s DEA registration to prescribe. These hours count within the total, but not toward the 12-hour risk-management requirement.

MD.detail: An initial prescriber applicant has a separate four-hour education requirement: two hours in pain management or addiction identification and two in opioid prescribing or dispensing practices. Document qualifying education within one year of initial licensure; prior qualifying professional education may satisfy it.

DO.detail: An initial prescriber applicant has a separate four-hour education requirement: two hours in pain management or addiction identification and two in opioid prescribing or dispensing practices. Document qualifying education within one year of initial licensure; prior qualifying professional education may satisfy it.

MD.detail: Two hours once, under the rules effective May 1, 2026. For a license issued before that date, the rule allows five years from licensure renewal; for a license issued on or after that date, five years from initial licensure; for a license reactivated on or after that date, five years from reactivation. Use the Board’s required curriculum. The hours count toward the general CME total.

DO.detail: Two hours once, under the rules effective May 1, 2026. For a license issued before that date, the rule allows five years from licensure renewal; for a license issued on or after that date, five years from initial licensure; for a license reactivated on or after that date, five years from reactivation. Use the Board’s required curriculum. The hours count toward the general CME total.

sections.title: Plan around your board’s calendar
paragraphs: A Pennsylvania DO renewal arrives two months before the MD renewal. If you hold licenses from both boards, keep separate completion windows and category totals even when an activity is acceptable to both.

For an MD, verify the certificate’s AMA PRA Category 1 designation. For a DO, verify AOA Category 1-A for the 20-hour minimum. A course topic that fits your practice is not enough to establish its category.

sections.title: First renewal, exemptions and separate training
paragraphs: A first-renewal exemption may apply to general CME. Ask your licensing board to confirm the exempt period for your license issue date before relying on it; specific training obligations require separate review.

Training-license, inactive-status and hardship provisions have their own conditions. A general CME exemption does not automatically remove child-abuse education or applicable prescriber obligations. Start a waiver request with your board before renewal.

sections.title: Records, reporting and carryover
paragraphs: Keep CME documentation for at least two years after renewal. Retain certificates and a dated activity log identifying the provider, topic, category and hours; the boards may request evidence in an audit.
For child-abuse training, confirm that your provider has reported completion before submitting renewal. Saving a certificate in a personal tracker does not perform that reporting.
Plan to earn your hours within the applicable biennium. Confirm any proposed use of earlier or surplus hours with your board before relying on them for a later renewal.

sections.title: What changed in 2026
paragraphs: The two-hour organ-and-tissue-donation requirement took effect May 1, 2026. Its deadline depends on whether your license predates that date, was issued afterward or was reactivated afterward. It is not another two-hour requirement at every renewal.

This guide was reviewed October 13, 2026 against the current regulations and board materials. The separate MD and DO category minimums, renewal dates and topic requirements remain central to planning.

faqs.question: How many hours of CME do Pennsylvania physicians need?
faqs.answer: MDs and DOs generally need 100 hours every two years. MDs need at least 20 AMA PRA Category 1 hours; DOs need at least 20 AOA Category 1-A hours.

faqs.question: Do Pennsylvania MDs and DOs renew on the same date?
faqs.answer: No. Regular MD renewal is December 31 of even-numbered years. Regular DO renewal is October 31 of even-numbered years.

faqs.question: Can child-abuse and opioid training count toward risk management?
faqs.answer: The Board guidance excludes the required child-abuse and opioid hours from the 12-hour patient-safety/risk-management requirement. They may still count toward the general total.

faqs.question: Is organ-donation training required at every renewal?
faqs.answer: No. It is a two-hour, one-time requirement. The May 1, 2026 rules use different five-year deadline triggers for existing, newly issued and reactivated licenses.

faqs.question: Does my CME tracker report child-abuse completion to Pennsylvania?
faqs.answer: The approved training provider must report completion electronically. A saved certificate or tracker entry does not replace the provider’s report.

faqs.question: Does a first-renewal exemption remove every training requirement?
faqs.answer: No. General CME exemptions and specific training obligations are separate. Confirm your initial-period treatment with your board, including child-abuse education and any applicable prescriber training.

faqs.question: How long should I keep Pennsylvania CME records?
faqs.answer: Both boards require documentation for at least two years after renewal. Keep evidence of the category, content, date and hours, including proof of one-time training.

sources.label: 49 Pa. Code § 16.19 — MD CME
sources.quote: At least 20 credit hours shall be completed in AMA PRA Category 1 approved activities.

sources.label: 49 Pa. Code § 25.271 — DO renewal and CME
Medical Board — unrestricted MD CME guidance
Medical Board — initial opioid education notice
Pennsylvania — Act 31 training and approved providers
ABC-MAP Act § 9.1 — initial and renewal opioid education

productNote: ClearCME helps organize certificates and renewal records. Confirm your MD or DO category minimum, initial-period exemption and organ-donation deadline with the Board. ClearCME does not submit official child-abuse course reports.

name: Illinois
title: Illinois CME Requirements for Physicians (MD & DO) | ClearCME
description: Illinois MD and DO CME requirements: 150 hours over three years, 60 formal hours, mandatory training, six-year topic clocks and controlled-substance renewal.
summary: Illinois uses a three-year physician renewal cycle with 150 hours of CME. Several smaller training requirements run on different clocks: some recur every renewal, some every six years, and opioid education follows your controlled-substance registration.

boards.label: MD and DO · Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation
boards.hours: 150 hours, including at least 60 formal hours
boards.cycle: The regular physician renewal date is July 31 every three years; the next regular renewal is July 31, 2029. IDFPR extended completion of the 2026 renewal process through August 31, 2026. The variance did not otherwise change CME requirements or the ordinary renewal cycle.
boards.credit: At least 60 hours in qualifying formal programs; up to 90 hours may come from qualifying informal CME. Document the program’s accreditation or qualifying sponsor. The CME pre-renewal period is the 36 months preceding July 31 in the renewal year.

MD.detail: One hour each renewal cycle, including the first renewal. This separate requirement still applies when you are exempt from the general CME total.

DO.detail: One hour each renewal cycle, including the first renewal. This separate requirement still applies when you are exempt from the general CME total.

MD.detail: One hour per renewal, beginning with the first renewal for which continuing education is required. From July 1, 2026, physicians who report providing maternal health care must include the specified maternal-health risk content in this hour.

DO.detail: One hour per renewal, beginning with the first renewal for which continuing education is required. From July 1, 2026, physicians who report providing maternal health care must include the specified maternal-health risk content in this hour.

MD.detail: One hour during each controlled-substance registration pre-renewal period. It applies to registered prescribers even if they do not prescribe opioids and at the first controlled-substance renewal. Qualifying training may count toward physician CME.

DO.detail: One hour during each controlled-substance registration pre-renewal period. It applies to registered prescribers even if they do not prescribe opioids and at the first controlled-substance renewal. Qualifying training may count toward physician CME.

MD.detail: One hour if you provide health care services to, and have direct patient interactions with, adults age 26 or older; repeat the course at least every six years. Newly licensed physicians should confirm first-renewal applicability with IDFPR before relying on a general CME exemption.

DO.detail: One hour if you provide health care services to, and have direct patient interactions with, adults age 26 or older; repeat the course at least every six years. Newly licensed physicians should confirm first-renewal applicability with IDFPR before relying on a general CME exemption.

MD.detail: One hour before the first renewal requiring continuing education on or after January 1, 2025, then at least once every six years. Keep its completion date separate from the recurring implicit-bias hour.

DO.detail: One hour before the first renewal requiring continuing education on or after January 1, 2025, then at least once every six years. Keep its completion date separate from the recurring implicit-bias hour.

MD.detail: Mandated reporters must complete initial training, including implicit bias, within three months of first serving in that role unless another applicable professional law sets the timeframe. Medical personnel who work with children repeat training at least every six years and attest to understanding reporting duties at renewal. Those who do not work with children may attest at renewal instead of repeating the training.

DO.detail: Mandated reporters must complete initial training, including implicit bias, within three months of first serving in that role unless another applicable professional law sets the timeframe. Medical personnel who work with children repeat training at least every six years and attest to understanding reporting duties at renewal. Those who do not work with children may attest at renewal instead of repeating the training.

sections.title: Formal and informal hours serve different parts of the total
paragraphs: The 60-hour formal minimum sits inside the 150-hour requirement. Qualifying formal education includes approved AMA, AOA and other programs recognized in the Illinois rule. Informal study can contribute to the remaining hours when it meets the rule’s definition.

Keep a dated record of informal activities that describes the learning, its relationship to professional practice and the time claimed. A general reading list without dates or hours is difficult to support at audit.

sections.title: First renewal and separate registrations
paragraphs: The general 150-hour requirement does not apply to the first physician renewal after original licensure. That exemption does not erase the separate sexual-harassment training obligation or the controlled-substance registration’s opioid education requirement.

Your physician license and controlled-substance registration are separate renewal obligations. Check both records before assuming that a course’s six-year interval or a physician exemption covers prescribing authorization.

sections.title: Carryover, records and hardship
paragraphs: The same hours cannot be used for more than one Illinois renewal period. Build each 36-month record from activities earned in that period.

Retain formal certificates and your informal activity log so that you can support the renewal attestation if IDFPR requests evidence. Keep one-time or six-year training documentation available for the later renewal where it matters.
The rule provides a hardship process. Submit a supported request before the license expires; a request alone is not approval.

sections.title: Recent changes and the next cycle
paragraphs: IDFPR extended completion of the 2026 physician renewal process through August 31, 2026. This one-cycle extension did not change the ordinary July 31 triennial schedule or other CME requirements.

Cultural-competency training applies to the first renewal requiring continuing education on or after January 1, 2025, then at least once every six years. Maternal-health content became part of the implicit-bias hour on July 1, 2026 for physicians who report providing maternal health care.
This guide was reviewed October 13, 2026. Opioid education remains due at each controlled-substance registration renewal; the six-year interval applies to other named topics.

faqs.question: How many CME hours do Illinois MDs and DOs need?
faqs.answer: Both generally need 150 hours during the three-year pre-renewal period, including at least 60 formal hours. Up to 90 may be qualifying informal CME.

faqs.question: When is Illinois physician renewal?
faqs.answer: The regular physician renewal date is July 31 every three years; the next regular renewal is July 31, 2029. IDFPR extended completion of the 2026 renewal process through August 31, 2026. The variance did not otherwise change CME requirements or the ordinary renewal cycle.

faqs.question: Is the first Illinois renewal exempt from all training?
faqs.answer: No. The general CME exemption does not remove sexual-harassment prevention or applicable opioid education for controlled-substance registration.

faqs.question: Is Illinois opioid training every six years?
faqs.answer: No. The one-hour safe-opioid-prescribing requirement is due during each controlled-substance registration pre-renewal period.

faqs.question: Who needs dementia education?
faqs.answer: One hour if you provide health care services to, and have direct patient interactions with, adults age 26 or older; repeat the course at least every six years. Newly licensed physicians should confirm first-renewal applicability with IDFPR before relying on a general CME exemption.

faqs.question: Does maternal-health training add another hour?
faqs.answer: For affected physicians, maternal-health content must be included in the existing one-hour implicit-bias course from July 1, 2026. It does not add a separate hour.

faqs.question: Can I reuse surplus CME at the next renewal?
faqs.answer: The Illinois rule does not allow the same hours to be used in more than one renewal period.

sources.label: 68 Ill. Adm. Code § 1285.110 — physician CME
sources.quote: In order to renew a license, a licensee shall be required to complete 150 hours of CME per prerenewal period.

sources.label: 720 ILCS 570/315.5 — safe opioid prescribing
sources.quote: every prescriber who is licensed to prescribe controlled substances shall, during the pre-renewal period, complete one hour of continuing education

sources.label: 68 Ill. Adm. Code Part 1130 — mandatory training
20 ILCS 2105/2105-15.7 — implicit bias and maternal health

productNote: Use ClearCME to keep certificates and renewal records together. Verify the 60-hour formal minimum, first-renewal exceptions and separate six-year or controlled-substance training clocks against IDFPR’s requirements.

name: Ohio
title: Ohio CME Requirements for Physicians (MD & DO) | ClearCME
description: Ohio physician CME requirements: 50 hours every two years, approved Category 1 pathways, duty-to-report training and the pain-clinic rule for MDs and DOs.
summary: Ohio MDs and DOs generally need 50 hours every two years, including a Board-approved hour on the duty to report misconduct. Physicians who own or provide care in a covered pain-management clinic have an additional topic requirement within that total.

boards.label: MD and DO · State Medical Board of Ohio
boards.cycle: Biennial renewal. Use the expiration on your Ohio license record to set the end of your reporting window.
boards.credit: Use the approved pathways in OAC 4731-10-02, including qualifying AMA or AOA Category 1 CME. The rule also addresses approved training and limited volunteer-service credit; ordinary Category 2 study is not the standard renewal pathway.

MD.detail: At least one hour of Board-approved training every renewal period. It counts toward the 50-hour total. Confirm that the specific activity is approved for Ohio’s duty-to-report requirement.

DO.detail: At least one hour of Board-approved training every renewal period. It counts toward the 50-hour total. Confirm that the specific activity is approved for Ohio’s duty-to-report requirement.

topics.title: Pain medicine for covered pain-management clinics

MD.detail: Physician owners and physicians providing care at clinics covered by OAC 4731-29-01 need at least 20 hours of Category 1 CME in pain medicine every two years. The education must include one or more courses addressing addiction potential. Qualifying hours count toward the renewal total.

DO.detail: Physician owners and physicians providing care at clinics covered by OAC 4731-29-01 need at least 20 hours of Category 1 CME in pain medicine every two years. The education must include one or more courses addressing addiction potential. Qualifying hours count toward the renewal total.

sections.title: Count approved hours within your own renewal window
paragraphs: Ohio’s rule identifies the education pathways that count toward renewal. Check the accreditation on each certificate before adding it to your total. A course may be clinically valuable without qualifying for Ohio renewal.
The duty-to-report hour is part of the 50 hours. A generic ethics course does not automatically satisfy the Board-approved duty-to-report requirement.

sections.title: The pain-clinic rule depends on your practice setting
paragraphs: The 20-hour pain-medicine requirement applies to physician owners and physicians providing care at a pain-management clinic covered by the Ohio rule. It is not a universal 20-hour requirement for every physician who writes an opioid prescription.

The rule includes a definition of a covered clinic and exclusions for certain facilities. Confirm whether your practice falls within that definition, then retain documentation showing pain-medicine content and the required addiction component.

sections.title: First renewal, inactive practice and hardship
paragraphs: For a first or shortened registration period, confirm the hours assigned to your license directly with the Board before relying on a reduced total. Use the physician rules and your license record when planning that first renewal.
Retirement or practice outside Ohio does not itself remove the CME obligation when you continue to renew the license. A CME waiver is a separate Board decision.

A CME waiver for qualifying illness, accident or absence must be requested at least 60 days before the end of the registration period. Under the waiver rule, submit the renewal application only after the Board grants that waiver.

sections.title: Records and use across renewal periods
paragraphs: Keep certificates, activity dates, categories and a record of your Board-approved duty-to-report training. Ohio law provides for random CME audits. Physicians subject to the pain-clinic rule should also preserve evidence of the qualifying content.

Hours used to make up a deficiency from a previous registration period cannot also count toward the current period. Ask the Board before banking surplus hours for a later cycle; do not assume that an old certificate belongs in the current 50-hour total.

sections.title: Current rules and recent changes
paragraphs: The current physician CME rule requires 50 hours and the recurring duty-to-report hour. The pain-management-clinic rule reviewed for this guide has an effective date of January 31, 2026.
This guide was reviewed October 13, 2026. Federal DEA training remains a separate obligation tied to DEA registration, even when a qualifying course is also eligible for Ohio CME.

faqs.question: Do Ohio MDs and DOs have the same general CME total?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both use the 50-hour requirement for each two-year registration period under the physician CME rule.

faqs.question: Does every Ohio physician need duty-to-report education?
faqs.answer: The CME rule requires at least one hour of Board-approved duty-to-report education every renewal period. It is included in the general total.

faqs.question: Does an ordinary ethics course meet the duty-to-report requirement?
faqs.answer: Only if the specific activity is Board approved for that requirement. Check the approval before enrolling.

faqs.question: Who needs the 20-hour pain-medicine requirement?
faqs.answer: It applies to physician owners and physicians providing care at a pain-management clinic covered by OAC 4731-29-01. Review the rule’s facility definition and exclusions.

faqs.question: Are the pain-clinic hours added on top of 50?
faqs.answer: No. Qualifying pain-medicine hours count toward the renewal total, provided the category and content requirements are met.

faqs.question: Am I exempt if I practice only outside Ohio?
faqs.answer: Practicing elsewhere does not itself exempt a physician who renews an Ohio license. Retirement alone is also not an automatic CME exemption.

faqs.question: Can deficiency hours count for two periods?
faqs.answer: No. Hours used to cure a prior-period CME deficiency cannot also be counted in the current period.

sources.label: OAC 4731-10-02 — CME for renewal
sources.quote: During a registration period, a licensee shall be required to complete fifty hours of CME.

productNote: ClearCME helps organize your CME evidence. Confirm Board approval for duty-to-report training, any first-period adjustment and whether your practice is covered by the pain-clinic rule. A tracker does not grant a Board waiver.

name: New Jersey
title: New Jersey CME Requirements for Physicians (MD & DO) | ClearCME
description: New Jersey physician CME: 100 hours, 40 Category I, 2027 renewal training, cultural competency, carryover and MD/DO board sources.
summary: New Jersey MDs and DOs generally need 100 hours every two years, including at least 40 Category I hours. The cycle beginning July 1, 2025 includes sexual-misconduct prevention and, for physicians providing perinatal care, bias training.

boards.label: MD and DO · State Board of Medical Examiners
boards.hours: 100 hours, including at least 40 Category I
boards.cycle: Biennial renewal. New training requirements apply to the cycle beginning July 1, 2025 and the applicable 2027 physician renewal.
boards.credit: Category I and Category II activities recognized by the AMA, AOA, ACCME or another organization accepted by the Board. Up to 60 hours may be Category II.

MD.detail: Two Category I hours each biennial cycle, within the 40-hour Category I minimum.

DO.detail: Two Category I hours each biennial cycle, within the 40-hour Category I minimum.

MD.detail: One Category I hour each biennial cycle on responsible prescribing, alternatives, and the risks and signs of opioid abuse, addiction and diversion. The physician CME rule does not limit this requirement to DEA registrants.

DO.detail: One Category I hour each biennial cycle on responsible prescribing, alternatives, and the risks and signs of opioid abuse, addiction and diversion. The physician CME rule does not limit this requirement to DEA registrants.

MD.detail: Two Category I hours each biennial cycle beginning July 1, 2025. The activity must cover all seven Board-required content areas, including sensitive-examination consent, power dynamics, reporting and human trafficking. A generic ethics or workplace sexual-harassment course may not cover the required curriculum.

DO.detail: Two Category I hours each biennial cycle beginning July 1, 2025. The activity must cover all seven Board-required content areas, including sensitive-examination consent, power dynamics, reporting and human trafficking. A generic ethics or workplace sexual-harassment course may not cover the required curriculum.

MD.detail: One Category I hour each biennial cycle beginning July 1, 2025 if you provide perinatal treatment or care. The rule covers care during pregnancy, labor, delivery, postpartum and neonatal periods. The course must address the Board’s required curriculum on implicit and explicit bias in perinatal care.

DO.detail: One Category I hour each biennial cycle beginning July 1, 2025 if you provide perinatal treatment or care. The rule covers care during pregnancy, labor, delivery, postpartum and neonatal periods. The course must address the Board’s required curriculum on implicit and explicit bias in perinatal care.

MD.detail: Six hours once if you have not satisfied the Board’s cultural-competency requirement through qualifying medical-school instruction or Board-accepted equivalent education. CME must meet the Board’s accreditation rules and cover all six required topics. For physicians licensed before March 24, 2005 who still need this training, the hours are additional to the ordinary 100; later licensees may include qualifying hours in the general total.

DO.detail: Six hours once if you have not satisfied the Board’s cultural-competency requirement through qualifying medical-school instruction or Board-accepted equivalent education. CME must meet the Board’s accreditation rules and cover all six required topics. For physicians licensed before March 24, 2005 who still need this training, the hours are additional to the ordinary 100; later licensees may include qualifying hours in the general total.

sections.title: Build the 2025–2027 cycle around the required topics
paragraphs: The end-of-life, opioid, sexual-misconduct and applicable perinatal-care hours are designated Category I requirements. Keep their certificates within your Category I record and confirm the specific curriculum.

Sexual-misconduct prevention is distinct from workplace sexual-harassment training. New Jersey lists seven required content areas; a familiar course title does not establish that all seven are covered.

sections.title: Cultural competency and the first complete cycle
paragraphs: Cultural competency is a one-time requirement, not six more hours at every renewal. Physicians licensed on or after June 30, 2007 generally must satisfy it by the end of the next complete renewal cycle after licensure.

Training outside New Jersey medical schools is not automatically assumed to meet the six-topic curriculum. Keep course outlines with your certificate and obtain the Board’s determination when relying on equivalent professional-school or graduate medical education.
For CME, confirm the provider uses a qualifying designation (AMA Category 1, AOA Category 1-A, 1-B or 2-A, or AAFP Prescribed) and an approved sponsor, with all six required curriculum areas.

sections.title: First renewal and license status
paragraphs: Applicants for an initial license who completed accredited graduate medical education within the 12 months before licensure are exempt from CME for their initial biennial period. They must complete a Board-presented or Board-approved orientation within 24 months after licensure. Confirm your eligibility before relying on this exemption.

Before your first renewal or a change in license status, check the Board’s instructions for your specific license. Confirm the CME obligation directly with the Board before relying on reduced-fee, inactive or retired status.

sections.title: Carryover and audit records
paragraphs: A physician who earns more than 100 hours in a biennium may carry forward no more than 25 excess hours to the immediately following biennium. Keep the original completion dates and a record of which hours were applied to each period.

Retain CME documentation for six years after completion. For cultural competency, keep curriculum evidence as well as attendance certificates. Request any hardship relief through the Board before relying on it at renewal.

sections.title: Recent changes
paragraphs: The rules beginning with the July 1, 2025 biennium add two Category I hours of sexual-misconduct prevention and one Category I hour of perinatal-bias education for affected physicians. The Board’s current CME notice identifies the applicable 2027 renewal as the deadline for sexual-misconduct training.
This guide was reviewed October 13, 2026. The source list includes the Board’s current regulations gateway and the official 2025 adoption notices.

faqs.question: How many CME hours do New Jersey MDs and DOs need?
faqs.answer: Both generally need 100 hours every two years, including at least 40 Category I hours. The remaining hours may be qualifying Category I or II activities.

faqs.question: What is new for the 2027 renewal?
faqs.answer: The cycle beginning July 1, 2025 includes two Category I hours of sexual-misconduct prevention and one Category I hour of perinatal-bias training for physicians providing perinatal care.

faqs.question: Is cultural competency required every two years?
faqs.answer: No. It is a six-hour, one-time requirement with prior-education and waiver provisions. The Board’s curriculum and completion deadline still matter.

faqs.question: Do cultural-competency hours always count within the 100?
faqs.answer: Not always. For physicians licensed before March 24, 2005 who did not receive qualifying cultural-competency instruction in medical school, the required training is additional to the ordinary 100-hour total, subject to the Board’s equivalent-education waiver. Later licensees may include qualifying hours. Previously satisfied training does not need to be repeated.

faqs.question: Can I carry excess hours into my next renewal?
faqs.answer: Up to 25 excess hours may be carried into the immediately following biennium. Keep a clear record of how the hours are allocated.

faqs.question: Does not prescribing opioids remove the opioid hour?
faqs.answer: The general physician CME rule includes one Category I opioid-education hour without a DEA-registration exemption. Federal MATE training is a separate requirement.

faqs.question: How long should I keep CME evidence?
faqs.answer: Keep documentation for six years after completion. For topic-specific requirements, retain evidence of the required content as well as the hour count.

name: Massachusetts
title: Massachusetts CME Requirements for Physicians (MD & DO) | ClearCME
description: Massachusetts MD and DO CME: 50 hours under the current pilot, 10 risk-management hours, birthday renewal, one-time training and Board sources.
summary: Massachusetts currently uses a 50-hour CME pilot for the two-year physician renewal period. Ten hours must address risk management. Some training repeats each cycle, while implicit bias, end-of-life care and several other requirements are completed once.

boards.label: MD and DO · Board of Registration in Medicine
boards.hours: 50 hours under the current CME pilot, including 10 in risk management
boards.cycle: Biennial renewal on your birthday. Confirm the first renewal deadline in your Board license record, especially when initial registration is close to your birthday.
boards.credit: Category 1 or Category 2 under the pilot, without a fixed general Category 1 minimum. The 10 risk-management hours may also be Category 1 or 2. Most of the cycle’s hours must relate to your primary area of practice.

MD.detail: 10 hours each biennial renewal, within the 50-hour total. Category 1 or 2 activities may qualify under the pilot.

DO.detail: 10 hours each biennial renewal, within the 50-hour total. Category 1 or 2 activities may qualify under the pilot.

MD.detail: Two hours each renewal for studying the Board’s regulations, 243 CMR 1.00–3.00. These hours may count toward risk management.

DO.detail: Two hours each renewal for studying the Board’s regulations, 243 CMR 1.00–3.00. These hours may count toward risk management.

MD.detail: Three hours each renewal if you prescribe controlled substances. Keep the Massachusetts requirement separate from the federal DEA training obligation.

DO.detail: Three hours each renewal if you prescribe controlled substances. Keep the Massachusetts requirement separate from the federal DEA training obligation.

MD.detail: Two hours once, if not previously completed. Required for applications received on or after June 1, 2022; qualifying hours apply toward risk management.

DO.detail: Two hours once, if not previously completed. Required for applications received on or after June 1, 2022; qualifying hours apply toward risk management.

MD.detail: Two hours once, if not previously completed. Preserve the completion record so that you can document the requirement at later renewals.

DO.detail: Two hours once, if not previously completed. Preserve the completion record so that you can document the requirement at later renewals.

topics.title: Child abuse and domestic or sexual violence

MD.detail: Complete the required child-abuse recognition/reporting training and domestic/sexual-violence training once. Only a Massachusetts Department of Public Health-approved course fulfills the domestic/sexual-violence requirement. These are separate educational obligations; the Board’s table does not assign a universal hour total to them.

DO.detail: Complete the required child-abuse recognition/reporting training and domestic/sexual-violence training once. Only a Massachusetts Department of Public Health-approved course fulfills the domestic/sexual-violence requirement. These are separate educational obligations; the Board’s table does not assign a universal hour total to them.

MD.detail: One hour once for renewal if you serve adult populations and have not already completed it.

DO.detail: One hour once for renewal if you serve adult populations and have not already completed it.

MD.detail: Demonstrate EHR proficiency once. One route is three hours of Category 1 EHR education covering Meaningful Use core and menu objectives and clinical quality measures. The regulation also recognizes other proficiency pathways, specified exemptions and time-limited waivers. Applicable exemptions must be claimed each licensing cycle.

DO.detail: Demonstrate EHR proficiency once. One route is three hours of Category 1 EHR education covering Meaningful Use core and menu objectives and clinical quality measures. The regulation also recognizes other proficiency pathways, specified exemptions and time-limited waivers. Applicable exemptions must be claimed each licensing cycle.

sections.title: Why the current total is 50 hours
paragraphs: Policy 17-05 sets the operative pilot requirement at 50 hours until the Board incorporates the policy into a new regulation. The Board’s current pilot page and requirements table continue to use that total.

The codified general renewal rule still contains older 100-hour language. Read it together with the current pilot policy rather than using that older number alone to plan an ordinary full-license renewal.

sections.title: First renewal and other license types
paragraphs: For a first renewal period of one year or less, the regulation waives the basic CME total. For a period longer than one year but shorter than two, it requires half of the basic biennial requirement. Confirm how the current pilot and separate training requirements apply to your dates.

Full active, limited, temporary and inactive licenses do not share every requirement. Use the Board’s license-specific table, especially when changing status or returning to practice. The initial-licensure training checklist is also separate from an ordinary renewal total.

sections.title: Keep recurring and one-time training separate
paragraphs: Track the recurring risk-management, regulations-review and applicable opioid hours for each cycle. Keep permanent copies of one-time training evidence so you can demonstrate prior completion.

A topic can contribute to a broader total when the Board permits it: for example, qualifying implicit-bias education applies toward risk management. Count the underlying hours once in the 50-hour total even if they support more than one requirement.

sections.title: Records, carryover and hardship
paragraphs: Keep a log identifying the activity, completion date and hours. The Board requires retaining CME records for at least one full renewal cycle after the cycle in which you earned the hours.

Plan your ordinary hours within the renewal window. Confirm proposed carryover with the Board rather than assuming excess hours automatically transfer. Hours assigned to remedy a deficiency apply to the deficient period.

The regulation provides a waiver process for circumstances such as prolonged illness or inaccessible CME. Submit a CME waiver request at least 30 days before renewal. A waiver requires a Board determination; an application or tracker entry is not approval.

sections.title: Recent policy history
paragraphs: The operative CME pilot was last amended April 11, 2024. The two-hour implicit-bias requirement applies to applications received on or after June 1, 2022. The current framework combines the 50-hour pilot with the existing specialized training requirements.
This guide was reviewed October 13, 2026 against the Board’s policy, CME table, regulations and the birthday-renewal statute.

faqs.question: Does Massachusetts require 50 or 100 hours of CME?
faqs.answer: The current Board pilot requires 50 hours for the ordinary biennial full-license renewal. The codified regulation retains older 100-hour language, so read it with Policy 17-05.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum number of Category 1 hours?
faqs.answer: The current pilot allows the general 50 hours and the 10 risk-management hours to be Category 1 or 2 without a fixed split. Specific training pathways may impose their own category conditions.

faqs.question: When do Massachusetts physicians renew?
faqs.answer: Physicians generally renew every two years on their birthday. Confirm your first renewal deadline in your Board license record.

faqs.question: Is implicit-bias training required every renewal?
faqs.answer: No. The Board lists two hours once, if not previously completed, for applications received on or after June 1, 2022.

faqs.question: Who needs the three-hour opioid education requirement?
faqs.answer: Physicians who prescribe controlled substances need three hours each renewal. The federal DEA MATE Act has a separate one-time framework.

faqs.question: Must I take a three-hour EHR course if I already demonstrated proficiency?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The regulation provides several proficiency pathways, plus specified exemptions and time-limited waivers. A qualifying three-hour Category 1 course is one route. Applicable exemptions must be claimed each licensing cycle.

faqs.question: Can a short first renewal reduce the general total?
faqs.answer: The regulation provides no basic CME total for a first period of one year or less and half the basic biennial requirement for a period longer than one year but shorter than two. Separate training conditions still need review.
